label: input u in the first three original positions
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter u at original-phase steps 0, 1 or 2. Never fires on any other input token, and never at the delimiter or during copy (including when u is fed back during copy). Magnitude depends on position: about 0.9-1.0 of max at t=0 and t=1, about 0.5-0.65 at t=2 (t=2 holds 24% of the mass versus 38% each for t=0 and t=1). At t=3 there are rare, very weak activations (about 0.02-0.05 of max) on u, and nothing from t>=4 on. Whether u appeared earlier makes little difference to firing: a repeated u at t<=2 still fires, somewhat weaker. Dev: precision 1.0, recall 0.977, mass recall 0.999.

issues: No systematic gap. On the test split, precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives, recall is 0.978 and mass recall is 0.999. The only misses are 1139 very weak activations on u at t=3 (about 0.00-0.04 of max, 0.1% of the mass), which the explanation already mentions.

The dev profile matches the explanation: no activation at the delimiter or in the copy phase, none for t>=4, and the only token that ever fires is u. Mass share by t is 0.380, 0.378 and 0.241, as claimed.
Adding t=3 to the predicate drops precision to 0.77 (F1 0.873), so t<=2 is the right cutoff.
A repeated u at t<=2 (u already seen earlier) still fires every time: precision is 1.0 on 1655 steps, which supports the claim that history matters little.

The phase=='copy' check predicted 0 steps, so that predicate may be malformed and proves nothing by itself. The copy-phase claim rests instead on the profile (0 active of about 2.73M copy steps) and the 0 false positives.
